Subject: Renewal discussion — higher SLOs & 24/7 oncall

Hi Logan,

We're coming up on our annual renewal for Cirrus Health and procurement asked me to kick off a conversation about moving to a higher support tier and formalizing stricter latency SLOs. We've been very happy with Redwood's uptime, but our product team is forecasting a step-change in peak traffic next quarter and they want: 

- formal P99 latency target of <= 200ms for inference requests to our production endpoint (current model: open-llama-70b-fp16),
- 24/7 oncall escalation (phone + Slack) for Sev1 incidents,
- guaranteed burst capacity for 2x current peak TPS for up to 6 hours/day,
- SOC2 evidence and audit logs retention tweak to 12 months (we will need this for our compliance folder).

I've attached a short SLO_Request doc that summarizes requirements and include procurement on the thread to coordinate PO timing. We're aiming to finalize terms by July 20 so engineering can schedule the performance changes. Can you share a preliminary commercial estimate and high-level ops plan (routing/fallback, canaries, oncall handoff)? Also flag any technical constraints if the requested SLOs are ambiguous with model/quantization choices.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Director of Platform Engineering
Cirrus Health

Thanks Logan — adding a few technical constraints and a concrete proposal so procurement has something to review.

Summary of constraints/assumptions:
- Model: open-llama-70b-fp16 (no quantization) — p99 <= 200ms depends heavily on sequence length and model batch sizing. If Cirrus is willing to use an 8-bit quantized variant we can shave ~30-40% latency at similar quality for many prompts.
- Traffic profile: need 99th percentile request size and a 7-day peak TPS sample to size KV cache and batch windows.
- Deployment topology recommended: Dedicated Reserved Pool (DRP) sized for baseline throughput + Autoscale Burst (ASB) for 2x peak. DRP ensures consistent p95; ASB covers brief demand spikes.

Operational changes to satisfy SLA:
- 24/7 oncall: Primary oncall from Redwood's Site Reliability team with an on-call runbook and 15-minute acknowledgement time for Sev1, and escalation to Engineering lead within 60 minutes.
- Canary rollout: New model/quantization and routing changes deployed to 5% traffic for 24 hours, monitor delta in latency and token-cost.
- Fallback: Automatic route to a slightly lower-capacity model variant if p99 crosses threshold, with graceful degradation and clear audit logs.

High-level sizing & cost ballpark (examples for discussion):
- Baseline: DRP sized to current sustained throughput = X GPUs (baseline invoice).
- Burst: ASB to cover 2x peak for 6 hrs/day = additional ephemeral GPUs; estimated extra monthly run-rate = ~+40% on top of baseline.
- 24/7 oncall + dedicated SRE rotation = flat monthly support fee (example: $8k/mo) or converted into higher unit price under committed term.

What I need from Cirrus to firm this up:
- 7-day traffic dump (timestamps, TPS, median/95/99 seq length)
- Confirmation whether quality tests accept 8-bit quantization candidate (I can run a small eval set).

Attaching a draft amendment (v2) with staged SLA language we can iterate on.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Amendment_v2.docx
